label: words
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: septic tank
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (11 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 10 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- A family septic tank often holds around 1,000 gallons, the usual minimum for a three-bedroom home.
- In a septic tank solids settle to the bottom as sludge while fats, oil and grease float to the top as scum
- A household septic tank is typically pumped every 3 to 5 years
- About one in five US homes uses a septic system.

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: the pit is dug and the toilet pipe grows into it. actions: dig dig (on "dig"); inlet grow (on "pipe"); inlet flow show (on "pipe")
   idea: you dig a pit behind the house and run the toilet pipe into it
   cue words: "dig", "pipe"
2. problem
   on screen: brown sewage fills the pit and spills onto the lawn. actions: sewage flood (on "fills"); sewage dirty (on "fills"); spill start (on "spills"); puddles rise (on "spills")
   idea: the pit fills with raw sewage and spills over onto the lawn
   cue words: "fills", "spills"
3. fix1
   on screen: a concrete tank appears, fills, and sludge sinks to its floor. actions: spill stop (on "So"); puddles dry (on "So"); sewage hide (on "tank"); tank show (on "tank"); tank fill (on "tank"); tank sink (on "sink")
   idea: a concrete tank holds it, and the heavy solids sink to the floor as sludge
   cue words: "So", "tank", "sink"
   its fact: A family septic tank often holds around 1,000 gallons, the usual minimum for a three-bedroom home.
4. problem2
   on screen: a dark scum layer floats up to the top. actions: tank float (on "float")
   idea: but grease and fat float up into a thick scum layer on top
   cue words: "float"
   its fact: In a septic tank solids settle to the bottom as sludge while fats, oil and grease float to the top as scum
5. fix2
   on screen: a T outlet pipe grows and clear water runs out of it. actions: outlet grow (on "pipe"); tank clear (on "clear"); outlet flow show (on "clear")
   idea: a T-shaped outlet pipe takes only the clear middle water out
   cue words: "pipe", "clear"
6. problem3
   on screen: puddles spread over the lawn at the pipe's end. actions: wet puddles rise (on "lawn")
   idea: dumped in one spot, that water turns the lawn into a swamp
   cue words: "lawn"
7. fix3
   on screen: a gravel bed and a holed pipe appear, water spreads and soaks down. actions: field grow (on "gravel"); field pipe grow (on "pipes"); field flow show (on "soaks"); field wet (on "soaks"); soak show (on "soaks"); soak arrows show (on "soaks"); wet puddles dry (on "soaks")
   idea: holed pipes in a gravel bed spread it out so the soil soaks it up
   cue words: "gravel", "pipes", "soaks"
8. name
   on screen: an outline traces the tank. actions: tank outline show (on "septic")
   idea: this is a septic tank
   cue words: "septic"
   its fact: About one in five US homes uses a septic system.
9. fact
   on screen: a years counter ticks up beside the tank as sludge piles higher. actions: tank outline hide (on "Sludge"); tank sink (on "Sludge"); stand show (on "pumped"); years show (on "pumped"); years count (on "every")
   idea: sludge keeps building, so the tank is pumped out every 3 to 5 years
   cue words: "Sludge", "pumped", "every", "3"
   its fact: A household septic tank is typically pumped every 3 to 5 years
10. finish
   on screen: a riser lid pops up and grass covers the tank. actions: years hide (on "Add"); soak arrows hide (on "Add"); soak hide (on "Add"); field flow hide (on "Add"); outlet flow hide (on "Add"); inlet flow hide (on "Add"); riser grow (on "lid"); lid show (on "lid"); dig refill (on "grass"); cap soil grow (on "grass"); cap grass grow (on "grass")
   idea: a riser lid and the grass go back on top
   cue words: "Add", "lid", "grass"
11. congrats
   on screen: calm lawn over the tank with its lid and the drain field
   idea: you have built a septic tank
   cue words: (none)
